verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Screaming Frog SEO Spider, crawl an owned site locally, inspect technical signals, and export raw audit data. The hard boundary is years of crawl edge cases, javascript rendering, integrations, and desktop performance, plus crawl scale, rule depth, and operational polish.
coreLoopDIY: Crawl a user-owned site locally, inspect HTML, rendered pages, and technical signals, explain prioritized issues, and export a reproducible audit.
requirements: permission to crawl the target site
whatYouLose: years of crawl edge cases, JavaScript rendering, integrations, and desktop performance
moatNotes: crawl scale, rule depth, and operational polish
ongoingBurden: robots handling, rendering, canonicalization, deduplication, crawl traps, rule maintenance, scheduling, storage, and false positives
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Screaming Frog SEO Spider because a crawler is buildable; professionals pay for years of edge-case handling and reports they can trust with clients. The recurring cost buys robots handling, rendering, canonicalization, deduplication, crawl traps, rule maintenance, scheduling, storage, and false positives, not just the visible interface.

alternatives.name: Crawly
alternatives.desc: Unlimited local crawling, JavaScript rendering and crawl diffs in a native Mac app; other operating systems get nothing.

facts.install: Download and install the native universal macOS app
facts.engines: A local MCP server connects to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf and other MCP clients
facts.dataFormat: Crawl projects and history live in a local SQLite database on the Mac; there is no hosted account or cloud sync
facts.gapVsPaid: It is macOS-only, lacks JavaScript rendering and offers far fewer crawl controls, extraction options, reports and integrations than Screaming Frog.

alternatives.name: FreeCrawl
alternatives.desc: A finished desktop crawler with 200 checks, JavaScript rendering, projects and exports; unusually close to the actual frog.

facts.install: Windows installer or portable build, macOS DMG, or Linux AppImage, deb or rpm
facts.engines: Optional OpenAI, Anthropic and local Ollama; optional GSC, GA4, PageSpeed, Ahrefs, Moz, Semrush, Majestic and MCP connections
facts.dataFormat: Local SQLite WAL project files (.seoproject), optionally AES-256-GCM encrypted; exports include Excel, CSV, JSON, XML, HTML, sitemaps, Google Sheets and BigQuery
facts.gapVsPaid: It is less battle-tested and has fewer mature configuration, extraction and integration workflows than Screaming Frog.
facts.setupBlocker: The prebuilt apps install normally, but the macOS build may require bypassing Gatekeeper for an unsigned application

alternatives.name: LibreCrawl
alternatives.desc: An unlimited browser-based crawler with JavaScript rendering; free, capable and one Docker stack away from useful.

facts.install: Docker Compose, or a Python environment plus Playwright
facts.dataFormat: Settings live in browser localStorage; each browser session has isolated crawl data that expires after one hour unless exported as CSV, JSON or XML
facts.gapVsPaid: It requires a Docker or Python and Playwright stack and offers less advanced crawl configuration, exports and integrations.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker or Python plus Playwright is required, and local mode has no authentication unless the operator adds it

alternatives.name: Screaming Frog SEO Spider Free
alternatives.desc: The same frog, permanently free for 500 URLs; JavaScript rendering, saved crawls and scheduling stay licensed.

facts.install: Native Windows, macOS or Linux installer
facts.dataFormat: Crawl data lives in the local running session and can be exported to spreadsheets; the free edition cannot save and reopen crawl projects
facts.gapVsPaid: The permanent free edition stops at 500 URLs and withholds JavaScript rendering, saved crawls, scheduling, custom extraction and API integrations.

alternatives.name: SEOnaut
alternatives.desc: A workmanlike crawler with issue severity, audit history and exports; less microscope, more dependable checklist.

facts.install: Docker Compose with MySQL 8.4, then expose the web UI behind HTTPS
facts.dataFormat: Sites, crawl results and audit history live in the self-hosted MySQL database
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a dependable checklist crawler but gives up Screaming Frog's raw-data depth, granular configuration, extraction and integration breadth.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker, MySQL and a reverse proxy are required; its default exposed port is plain HTTP

alternatives.name: SiteOne Crawler
alternatives.desc: A proper cross-platform crawler with JavaScript rendering, reports and raw exports; no license key hiding under the lily pad.

facts.install: Download a prebuilt desktop or CLI binary for Windows, macOS or Linux
facts.engines: Optional OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
facts.dataFormat: Runs locally and writes project results plus HTML, JSON or text reports and exports to the user's disk
facts.gapVsPaid: It covers the common audit job, but it still has fewer deeply mature crawl controls, custom extraction workflows and integrations than Screaming Frog.
facts.setupBlocker: None for ordinary crawling; JavaScript rendering needs Chrome or Chromium, or the one-time headless-shell download

rejectedAlternatives.name: RustySEO
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The feature list is excellent; v0.3.9, unsigned binaries and an explicit buggy warning make it a watchlist item.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the SEO Spider licence plan and a single-site audit tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Screaming Frog SEO Spider in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, Playwright, and an HTMX interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: crawl a user-owned site locally, inspect HTML, rendered pages, and technical signals, explain prioritized issues, and export a reproducible audit.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Require an explicit ownership or permission acknowledgement before a crawl starts.
Respect robots.txt, rate limits, canonical URLs, nofollow, redirects, and a configurable URL cap.
Collect status, title, description, headings, canonical, robots, links, images, structured data, and rendered text.
Detect duplicates, orphan candidates, broken links, redirect chains, missing metadata, and indexability conflicts.
Show every issue with affected URLs, evidence, severity, and a concrete remediation note.
Export crawl data and issues to CSV plus a self-contained HTML report.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out crawling sites without permission.
Deliberately leave out web-scale backlink or keyword datasets.
Deliberately leave out automated changes to production websites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
